summary: Flathead County lookout cab from 1931, destroyed in 1957 per firelookout.com; staffed in 1934 and 1951 per newspapers quoted on Forest Lookouts; site today undocumented.

facts.status_note: Cab destroyed in 1957 per firelookout.com; no source we read describes what remains at the site today

events.note: Man stationed at the lookout during the fire season; a September 22, 1934 item (The Daily Inter Lake, quoted on Forest Lookouts) says the lookout had closed for the year
Fire danger required manning the lookout (Hungry Horse News, quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Firelookout.com says destroyed; no cause given

evidence.supports: built 1931 as an L-4 cab; destroyed 1957
site listed under the Flathead National Forest
1934 item attributed to The Daily Inter Lake
Charles Burtsfield stationed at the lookout during the 1934 fire season
evidence.quote: Charles Burtsfield, who has been stationed at the lookout station on Moose Peak during the fire season

evidence.supports: lookout closed for the year (1934 item)
evidence.quote: The lookout having been closed for this year.

evidence.supports: 1951 item attributed to the Hungry Horse News
fire danger made manning the lookout necessary in August 1951
Frank Kohoutek made a 12-mile hike to the 7,521 foot peak in 1951; elevation disagreement
evidence.quote: Frank Kohoutek made the 12 mile hike Sunday to the 7,521 foot high peak

evidence.supports: Montana list places the site in Flathead County as a ground lookout that is gone

corrections.proposed: no height found in any source read; remove the value
corrections.why: The cited page describes a 1931 L-4 cab and gives no tower height, and 158.8 m is not plausible for a cab of this kind

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 158.8 is not supported by any source read; see corrections. That correction applies to the site record outside these two files, which this check did not edit. Elevation disagrees: 7,531 ft (firelookout.com) vs 7,521 ft (1951 newspaper quoted on Forest Lookouts); both are kept in the story. The 1934 item calls it Moose Peak. The Sanders County Moose Peak on the FFLA list is a different site (Tower, Gone). The Ron Kemnow credit does not appear on the Forest Lookouts page, so it was dropped from the sources. No photo found: the image on the Forest Lookouts pages is shared across pages and was not checked as a lookout photo, so not used. Searches found no other source describing the site.
